When the sun came out later in the morning, the cave at the base of the climb was dislodging fist size rocks. P2 - climbed the left hand line of the curtain, found a breakable crust on low angle features, but steeper features climbed well overall.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Did a tour around the Bow Summit area today and got 3 laps in. A bit better than expected, had some fresh snow and good coverage with a supportive base keeping you off the rocks. There's a widespread rain-crust that is very supportive until you get to around treeline where you start to crunch through. Approx 5cm of fresh dry and light snow atop the crust, more as you got higher, the kind of…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Recent rain crust very evident on the way upto treeline, but was definitly beggining to thin out at our highpoint (just short of 2400m). some evidence of wind deposition onthe eastern side of trees and rock features at treeline and up

reports.title: Stem and Bow summit bowl
reports.comment: quick: Skied one lap in the bow summit bowl. HS 70cm in the bowl most of the snow pack with the exception of the crust is 4F firm. 15cms of fresh snow sitting on top of the nov 5. crust. The Crust is very supportive so it makes for good skiing right now. Crust is really defined untill well into the alpine then it shifts to a pencil frim layer.  Skied the stem as well which is filled in but sharky …

reports.title: Bow summit south glades/tree chutes
reports.comment: quick: We saw an old slab 40m across in bowl south of the tree chutes probably from earlier this week but unsure. Many people riding flower couloir but we went for mellower terrain as first day of the season

reports.title: Mount Patterson-Middle Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: We skied the Middle Couloir off Mount Patterson. Our main concerns were windslab and the rain crust being a poor bonding surface that would produce loose dry avalanches based on the snow density of the new snow fallen Wednesday pm to Friday am. This couloir is fairly sheltered and steep at the top. 

The day was truly extreme: extremely good ski quality and extremely bad ski quality. The BT…

reports.comment:
quick: We rode the Helen Shoulder area, riding both the NE aspects and the west side. We dug a pit on the NE aspect, recording a 75 cm snow depth, though in a relatively well protected area at 2350m on a 37 degree slope. Air temperature was -3 and snow temperature was -8.

There was 12cm of fresh snow on top of a minor crust of well consolidated snow. That layer was about 25 cm with a rock hard cr…

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the glades at bow summit. Found good sheltered powder turns. 

Was a busy day with parties on Flower Couilor and the bowl to the RH side.

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: quick: Skied the treeline terrain at observation sub peak around 2400m. Today it was snowing S-1 throughout the day with overcast to broken skies. Wind was light to moderate with signs of blowing snow. It snowed 2-4cms through the day. We did not note any new avalanches. Skiing was good with 20cms of new snow overlying a breakable crust at this elevation. We did not see signs of significant WSL at…

reports.comment: quick: Nov 5 rain crust supportive to boots at this elevation and aspect. Made for good dust on crust skiing, with 30cms of fist density pow overlying the crust. We were wary of any stiff windlsab atop the crust, however even in small lee features where we expected stiff windlsab, we found a density increase to only 4F, surprising given moderate-strong winds at high elevations night previously. reports.title: Mosquito creek
reports.comment:
quick: Skied up mosquito creek drainage. Towards oxo/dolomite pass area. Good skin track in through the trees. 

At 2100 the snow was deeper and the rain crust was noticeable 10-20cm down.  HS 60cm. -7c lightly snowing and overcast. 

Mod-strong Westerly winds. Observed three size 1 dry loose (LD) avalanche from the E side of the dolomite shoulder that had run recently. / avalanche: Three size 1 L…

reports.title: Sastrugi
reports.comment: quick: Sastrugi and snow drifts from north wind on upper ridge. Boot deep powder on bottom half of ridge. Light snow all day. Temperature just below zero.

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment:
quick: Ski quality great today. Lots of new snow that gets more wind affected as you climb out above the trees. Dug a pit on west facing slope at approx 2300m and had 2 layers fail, one 45cm down on our 8th tap and one 25cm down on 12th tap. We chose to ski moderate slopes all under 30 degrees. 

Will try to get more scientific with my reports as the season goes. Stay safe, everyone.

reports.title: Bow Glacier
reports.comment:
quick: skied upto the bow glacier

Lake not fully frozen so struck mainly to the summer trail

Canyon has some areas of open water which are avoidable 

Moraines above canyon have thin snow coverage

Glacier snow depth was on average 130cm and filled in. The higher we went up the glacier the more wind affected the snow was. The lower slopes skied well.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Skied Crowfoot Glades (#59 in the guidebook) yesterday. Approach is in good shape. 

About 20cm on the rain crust which is still making uphill and downhill travel nice. New snow was unconsolidated and moving much on the crust. No significant wind affect in that sheltered area but we noticed plenty up high. Coverage is decent for mid Nov.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Did a few laps in the tree triangle at Crowfoot Glades. -5 at the car 0950am. About 10cm of new snow overnight. 

Good ski quality with the Nov 5 crust providing good support. Things were getting a bit choppy towards mid day and snow started to feel heavier then. 

No signs of instability where we skied. Noticed some heavy drifting high up on Bowcrow Wall. / weather: Indication of strong wi…

reports.title: Bow Summit Bowl & South Shoulder Tree Chutes
reports.comment: quick: Carefully stepped out into the Bow Summit bowl this morning. A few rock sharks still hidden, but was pleasantly surprised by the quality of turns this early in the season. Also, skied the southern most tree chute and was able to pick our way through the lower trees to the flats by the Bow River with a bit of side slipping and careful tree/twig/log navigation. / avalanche: Ski cut a small Si…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Great skiing at Bow Summit today. HS 83cm at treeline. CTM20 SC on basal facets. No reaction on Nov 5 rain crust. Snowing steadily all day, heavy at times. Highway was a mess, 25-30 cm on road, but ploughed by afternoon. A small, (but noisy) storm snow release down The Stem around 3:00pm that ran mid path.

Another collapse at 40 at CT13.  Collapse with two tests at 15 on November crust and at 17 (7th elbow tap) failed to ground. reports.title: Crowfoot Galdes
reports.comment: quick: Skied crowfoot glades today. Ski quality was excellent with 30+cms of storm snow. We saw moderate SP results on the Nov rain crust (down 70cm) and easy RP results on the storm snow (30cms). We triggered a sz 1 as noted on steep treeline terrain on the storm snow interface. reports.title: Puzzle
reports.comment:
quick: Skied a couple laps on puzzle ramp.
Variable coverage with best skiing in cross loaded features. Avoided wind loaded convexities which showed easy hand shear results down 35cm on facets below a buried wind slab. reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Good quality riding and nice temps made for an enjoyable Saturday at Crystal Ridge. Lots of backcountry users (skiers, splitboarders, and snowshoers) out with 18 vehicles at the Crowfoot Glacier Lookout at 10am. reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Very nice day up at Crystal Ridge. Good skiing in trees. Wind Slabs ready to let go on steeper slopes. Cracking on skin track. Lots of snowshoers stepping on skin tracks creating tough grip in spots.

reports.title: Bow Hut Weekend
reports.comment: quick: Bow Hut Weekend - Spent a couple of nights at Bow Hut, quite good for November. It snowed all day Friday, at times heavy, moderate winds. Mod winds Saturday, trace amounts of snow, high winds Sunday, no new snow. Lots of snow transport all weekend but we didn't find as much windslab as we expected. reports.comment:

reports.title: Dolomite shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Some whumpfing on skin track, spotted a size 1.5 off of Noseeum (see photo) in high alpine area. 

Snow pack was extremely variable, dust on scree on windward at alpine with wind effect and slab, 40-60 cm in sheltered and 120 in leeward. Skin track after the decision point between Oxo and dolomite is a bit ambitious unless you love (or want more practice in) kick turns and the out is a bit …

reports.title: Mt Thompson W benches
reports.comment: quick: Took a walk up to the benched area below Mt Thompson / Portal peak. the snow up to the top of the tress was powder sitting on the nov 5 crust, made for good travel and  riding from there down. Above there was a mixed bag of windslabs, crusts and rocks with thin powder over rocks in some areas.

reports.title: West Nile area
reports.comment: quick: We found between 40cm (2100m) -1m (2500m) of snow sitting on top of November raincrust. Also wind affected, non-reactive slab (between 3-10cm) on different aspects. Signs of facets under new snow, gave way easily in certain areas. No cracking or whumpf observed. Old debris from previous cycle but no avalanches heard or seen.

reports.title: Grand Daddy Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Followed skin tracks from Mosquito Creek Hostel until tree line. River Crossing was frozen and passable. Alpine had evidence of cross loading and couloir fan had some large avalanche debris which seemed quite old. Our uptrack went up lookers left of the couloir runout. reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Couple of laps at Crowfoot Glades today, we skied the road side chute #2 and then the Tree Triangle. Good snow and skiing conditions with approx. 10/15cm of fresh snow in the past 48hrs hours. Significant wind transport happening everywhere. Around 2100m on the SW aspect there were prominent wind affected areas in open treed areas. Some places scoured almost to ground with big drifts on the lee side of features. reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Snow seemed quite stable though we were only on fairly mellow slopes.Crowfoot glades has been quite tracked out at least where we were on the pillow drainage. I would guess around 50 people passed through for at least one lap today.

reports.title: Observation Subpeak
reports.comment:
quick: Headed up the drainage between Cirque and Observation subpeak and got a few turns in on the low angle slopes on the south aspect of subpeak. 

Ski cut some cornices overhanging a small gully on the south aspect of the subpeak which didn't trigger any slabs. Saw debris from a size 2 on the north aspect of Cirque which looked a few days old, hard to tell with the recent winds. Appeared to be …

reports.title: Puzzle Ramp
reports.comment:
quick: Skied trees and alpine at Puzzle Peak along with several other parties. Managed to find some excellent alpine turns by picking blown-in lanes on the ramp, where HS varied from 20 to 120. Lots of rocks and boulders. Trees below are deep powder HS of 80-130+.

Most alpine aspects were heavily wind affected, with stripped ridges and ribs on all south and west aspects. Significant deposition ob…

reports.title: Out for a walk behind Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: weather: Bluebird with a couple of small clouds here and there. - 1C at the cars and some solar effect on south facing higher angle slopes in the morning. A little after 2pm temps started dropping and wind died down. / snowpack: There's been a fair bit of wind above treeline, but we found some great low angle turns at treeline.

reports.title: Na size 2.5 avalanche, Dolomite Peak, Banff NP
reports.comment: avalanche: A large natural avalanche was observed on Dolomite Peak around 1100 AM. It occurred in a SW facing cross loaded alpine gully at about 2500 m, and appears to have failed on the Nov 5 crust/facet combo. Parks Canada Visitor Safety

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: avalanche: Triggered a sz 1 to 1.5 avalanche in the Crystal Ridge area. The weak layer let go under/in front of first member of group on a sparsely treed slope while on the uptrack just after emerging from a small grouping of trees. No one was caught in the avalanche.

reports.title: West Nile/Bow View
reports.comment: quick: Skied West Nile area and attempted accessing Bow View ridge, after a hasty pit with Mod hand shear results on the Nov 5th I pulled the pin. Skiing was excellent with 20-30 cm ski pen and now wind effect or other tracks. I did get a couple of settlement BTL where the snowpack was considerably thinner. HS was 120cm at TL tapering to 60cm BTL, Nov 5th down 60cm at TL.

reports.title: Bow summit skiing
reports.comment:
quick: Great ski conditions at bow summit with about 30cm of low density lightly wind affected powder atop what ever windslabs had been pushed around and present Friday.

Cold day, signs of slab avalanches likely from Friday's winds present on some west faces like (dolomite). Lots of blowing snow today. The area was very busy as per usual.

No signs of instability while skiing up or skiing.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Skied 3 excellent laps in the Helen Shoulder zone today. First two were on the backside, heading towards Helen Creek (2350-2100m) where we skied from the low alpine off the ridge into mellow rolling open trees and finally into a steep pillow zone. Our last lap was through the burn on the south side, where we found great snow all the way back to the access trees. The lower trees have enough …

Skied a fan feature and some pillows all the way down to the denser trees towards the creek. Really good ski quality there. reports.title: Wapta
reports.comment: quick: Did a quick lap on the Wapta/Bow Hut Glacier with our high point being around 2750m. We found better than expected snow. Up on the icefield it was mostly wind pressed but it had patches of shallow powder. reports.title: West Nile/Grand Daddy Fan
reports.comment:
quick: Skied in the west Nile area today skiing the fan below granddaddy and the trees below. Ski quality was good but variable depending on if an area was lee or not with many non lee areas being fairly windswept hard snow.

reports.title: Observation sub peak
reports.comment: quick: Went out to observation sub peak glades today, good snow below tree line. Above tree line was getting heavy/warm, saw pinwheels on some steep alpine faces. Dug a quick pit, compression test showed sudden fracture on nov crust at moderate to  hard Snow depth was about 80-90cm below treeline

reports.title: Patterson mini golf
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the lookers left mini golf line on Patterson. 

Plenty of evidence of wind affect in the chute. Wind slab up top prevented us from topping out. Booting was pretty unsupportive with variable foot pen from 40-120cm. The Nov crust seemed to be mostly turned to facets.

Inversion in the alpine but didn't notice any wind.

Ski quality ranged from very good to not very good with lots of bre…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Two consecutive days of ascending Dolomite Shoulder and descending East to the valley bottom. Ascent was as to be expected, wind effected sastrugi, and rocky. Descent however was great. Evidence of wind slabs on ridges, 20-30cm of powder albeit on a thin but solid base. No signs of cracking or any other avalanche activity.

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment: quick: Found decent skiing in the trees. Above treeline there were lots of small wind slabs. HS at treeline was 75cm

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Snow was good and stable such that we were able to ski some steeper aspects, a little wind affected in the Alpine. Noticed some surface hoar forming on S/SW facing aspects near the end of our the day (14:00). Temperature in the morning was -13C, warming to -2C at the car by the end of the day.

reports.title: Observation Subpeak South Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Toured gladed south aspect of Observation Subpeak South Ridge. Sheltered areas in treeline yielded blown in powder. Breakable sun crust in open trees. reports.title: Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: quick: Skied the lower slopes of Observation Sub Peak between 2200m and 2600m. The snowpack was extremely variable; some spots it was crusty, some places powder, other spots the snow was fully faceted to ground. The day started off sunny and warm but around noon the clouds rolled in and was mainly overcast. The winds were increasing while we were out.

reports.title: Grand Daddy Couloir
reports.comment:

reports.title: Helen Shoulder (the burn)
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the burn on Helen Shoulder. Snow felt heavier as the solar input increased. Overall good skiing conditions.

Many groups in the area enjoying the fresh snow. Some whumpfing on steeper aspects on skin up.

reports.title: Ice climbing: Uli's Revenge
reports.comment: quick: Rarely formed Uli's Revenge & With/without you. Variable ice conditions. View photo 2 for expanded view of overhead & approach slopes from Little Crowfoot.

reports.title: Cirque Peak - North Glacier
reports.comment: quick: We rode Cirque North glacier. Below 2600 m, good skiing, with 20 cm of powder/facets. Below treeline is still rough on the exit. Above, wind hammered slopes, with mix of soft slabs and crust. No signs of instability. Some older point releases to size 1 on south facing slopes.

reports.title: Helen shoulder and crystal ridge backside
reports.comment:
quick: Odd weather on Helen ridge with a slight inversion that seemed to be super elevation dependent. Get 5 m above it and dropped 5-10 degrees. 

Lots of surface hoar everywhere on both sides of Helen ridge, bigger down roadside. 

Most steep features on backside of crystal have sluffed with the recent snow. We skied the fan below sugar cube, dust on crust

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: No avalanches observed. Good skiing of 20 cm of faceting powered with supportive snowpack below. Pinwheels and tree bombs observed at treeline.

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Skied Dolomite shoulder. Saw evidence of growing Surface Hoar in and around 2200m. Recent storm snow skied great on top of the melt freeze crust. We saw no instability between the storm snow and crust. We did see evidence of steep alpine sloughing but was not stepping down at all.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge Area
reports.comment:
quick: The recent snow averaged anywhere from 10-30cm of ski penetration on a solid midpack. The surface was mostly facets, so no signs of slab formation.

The slough was defintiely running fast and running fairly far. It was put biggest concern on the day as we skied multiple laps near (not in) the sugar cube couloir and on the front side of Crystal Ridge.

-20C at 9AM and -14C at 3PM.

reports.title: Bow peak/crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: Went out to try  and summit bow peak. Made it to the saddle between bow peak and bowcrow. Bow peak is totally wind scoured and the winds we gusting to around 80 while we were there. Turned around because skiing down from the peak isn’t an option due to lack of snow. Skied pillows and trees below bow crow and then crowfoot glades. 40cm of fresh snow sitting on the old snow from early Decembe…

reports.title: Watch out for Momma Bear!!
reports.comment: quick: This area is closed because of a denning Grizzly!  Check the National Parks important bulletin for more details.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Mainly cloudy with some moderate wind in the morning and flurries in the afternoon. Dug a pit and cut some steeper slopes with no cracks or sluffing. Decided acceptable to ski steeper terrain after our first run. / snowpack: 20-30+ of powder overnight, 160cm snowpack. Progressive compression failure 40cm deep between 8-13 taps (avg. of three tests at a single test pit). No planar failure ob…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: 20+ overnight by Sunday morning. Local winds were out of the N and the N facing terrain on steeper aspects was stiffening on the surface. 5cm 4F above fist. May tighten up more if winds continue. Temps -5C and winds off and on ~20km/h N generally cloudy with some open pockets of sky.

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment:
quick: Great day out at crowfoot, rode the main runs and roadside chutes. 25-ish cm of storm snow on top of the previous 30/40cm from the past storm.

CT showed RP8 50cm down where the older storm snow has started to slab up. RP23 down 100cm on the weaker December layer. Nov weak layer is down about 140cm.

Snowing more when we left at 4pm.

reports.title: Hellen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Experienced multiple whumpfs in sheltered areas around the Hellen Shoulder burn.

reports.title: Skier remote avalanches on Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment:
avalanche: Observed two skier remote avalanches from a group of two skiing on Dolomite Ridge. 

The larger one appeared to be about 20 m from their ski tracks. It was a size 2, about 50 m wide, that stepped down to the basal crust/facet layer near the ground. The avalanche took out a slope with ski tracks from last week and the debris covered the edge of a common high exit traverse from the Dolomi…

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment:
quick: Was - 22c at the parking lot around 9am. - 13 at the car at 1pm. Winds were light in the morning at the car but moderate to strong winds had already started moving the new snow in the alpine upon arrival. By days end wind had picked up more in the alpine with plumes and large spindrifts visable on the drive home.

Skiing was great. Not many people, more cars at other areas. Soft wind loaded…

reports.title: Size 1.5 Skier Accidental, Observation Peak
reports.comment: avalanche: A Parks Canada staff member witnessed a skier triggered sz 1.5 on the lower slopes of Observation Peak from Highway 93N. The slab released above the group as they were setting their up track. At least one person was involved in the avalanche. No reported injuries and they skied away.

reports.title: Obs sub peak
reports.comment:
snowpack: SE aspect 2450m, HS 60cm.  20cm 1F windslab sitting on top multiple facet and slab layers.  Medium hand pit results, lots of settlements.  

SW aspect, 2500m, HS 60cm, 30cm 1F windslab sits on 10 cm F-4F facets overtop P hard crust.  Column failures upon isolation.  Repeatable results.

reports.title: Crowfoot glades - glacial moraine
reports.comment: snowpack: Still touchy out there, overall great day! Observed numerous size 1-2 loose dry slides come down over the glacier. Lots of wind up high but rather calm down low.

reports.title: Grizzly Closure
reports.comment:
quick: The signs and flagging are getting covered up by snow. 
Just a heads up for the Grizzly Closure! Check out the Parks Canada Important Bulletin!

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Closer to the top of tree line was more wind affected, bit crusty on the top layer. Skiing down below tree line was powdery, watch out for cliffs and small trees. Mosquito creek crossing could use more snow.

reports.title: Helen shoulder burn
reports.comment: quick: Toured up Helen shoulder and skied the open alpine run directly lookers left of the burn. On our way up through the trees we encountered around 10cm of soft snow. As we got into the alpine and out of the trees the wind affect was prevent on most aspects. Anything unsheltered was hard underneath with a few cm of snow on top making for punchy unpredictable turns. Felt multiple buried windslab…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Stuck to treeline and below, as the snow above treeline had a hard crust in some places. We skiied glades on the south and southeast facing slopes, with consistent boot-deep powder

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Good quality skiing and moderate trail breaking in sheltered trees.  Above TL and into the alpine, obviously wind affected with a mix of wind and solar crusts on full south aspects.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge N face

reports.title: Near Miss - Stay Diligent For Unsupported Features
reports.comment: incident: Near Miss - New rider accidently ski cut unsupported slope while trying to traverse around cliff band. No injuries, but some shaken nerves. Good reminder to avoid unsupported features, despite decreasing avalanche forecast.  Crown 45cm. 5m wide. Ran 3m.  I would have uploaded this earlier but the app wouldn't cooperate.

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment: quick: Light winds all day, very cold in the alpine,  fully supportive old wind slabs with 5-15cm of fresh snow on top. Only heard drumming in two spots on way up in wind scooped areas. good coverage in lower forest.

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: avalanche: On a blue bird day descending from Observation Sub Peak East, i trigger a slide.  At about 2700 m, on a cross loaded convex roll my ski cut triggered a small wind slab. reports.title: Cirque forepeak
reports.comment:
quick: Cold clear day at cirque forepeak, -22 @8am, -14 in alpine. No wind all day, very light winds noticed on surrounding summits as we skied out. 

CTM @2300, HS 90, 30 deg angle, SE aspect

20cm on a supportable crust in the alpine, fun powder at TL. No instabilities in the area noticed.

reports.title: Observation Peak
reports.comment: quick: Skied the tree triangle on the lower slopes of Observation Peak up to 2400m. Great skiing, no new avalanche activity seen or signs of instability noted where we skied. Sunny and calm conditions.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:

reports.title: Observation Sub-Peak Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Wild bushwack to tree line. Once at tree line and above skiing was awesome. reports.title: Patterson center couloir
reports.comment: quick: Went for Patterson center couloir today. River was frozen but a bit of a bushwhack to get to the fan of the couloir. We did notice some small shooting cracks while up tracking in a slide path at treeline for one or 2 switchbacks. reports.title: Bow to yoho
reports.comment:
quick: Completed the bow to yoho traverse from the 28th to the 30th.

Our group camped both nights, the huts are locked but the washrooms are open!

reports.title: Dolomite peak circuit
reports.comment: quick: Skiied the dolomite peak circuit. Run down to Kathryn lake was fast with 4cm of fluffy fresh snow on a supportive (wind?) crust. Rest of the circuit was a great day out with excellent weather, no wind and sun all day. One whumpf observed on the way up to the puzzel dolomite col (pin location) and a couple small sluffs observed high up on the south east aspect of Dolomite.  No other avalanch…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Pleasant day at Bow Summit. We skied the upper parts of the roadside paths and the bowl and made sure to stay well north of the bear closure. No signs of instability noted. Area is quite tracked but still soft. Minor wind affect around the ridge and some crystals forming. -10 at the car. 

Nice tracks coming out of Flower which looked to be in good shape. Pac Man also looked to be in reason…

reports.title: Crystal Ridge Backside/Sugar Cube
reports.comment:
quick: Had a good day in the Crystal Ridge backside area, including skiing Sugar Cube couloir. Snow as mostly soft powder on top of a stiffer but still soft interface. No signs of instability were noted throughout the day. Conducted a few hand shears in the top 30cms of snowpack, producing no significant results. The powder required minimal sluff management in confined terrain.

Exiting through th…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: snowpack: Snowpack test failed planar clean CTH 26 down 30 cms. Failed planar clean CTH 27 down 50. Appeared both failures were on the two December crusts. The snow felt stable, powder skiing on top of supportive crust. No signs of instability noted.

reports.title: Bow Peak
reports.comment:
avalanche: Accidentally triggered surface hoar on an unsupported pillow. Down 50cm. Not found as soon as we got into wind exposed areas.

Old hard surface from sloughs running in a couloir was providing a good bed surface for thin slabs of new snow that were warming up with the day. / weather: Blowing snow causing some spindrift at times. Most of the blowing snow getting blown beyond start zones o…

reports.title: Observation Glades
reports.comment: snowpack: Dug a pit on a 30 degree aspect just above tree line below observation peak. Failed sudden clean planar CTH 13 down 30 cms. Failed crusty resistant CTH 30 on November rain crust. Decided not to go up any higher due to test result. No instabilities observed below tree line.

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Dolomite shoulder provided excellent skiing. Majority of the first bowl and pillow line are skied out. We ventured up to Puzzle ramp but coverage is still very minimal and a lot of sharks out there. Storm was just coming in and there was very flat light, stuck to slopes with trees and rocks for markers.

reports.title: Bow Lake Practice Slopes
reports.comment: quick: A lovely day skiing the practice slopes at Bow Lake. Skied nearly all the obvious lines. Prior groups had been in the area likely a day or two prior but lots of fluffy still to be found. Dug a pit near the upper glades area and found a buried rain crust approx 20cm deep. reports.title: Bow Summit Powder Day
reports.comment: quick: Quiet day at Bow Summit with only 4 cars at the parking lot. Temps hovered between-4 to -7. 20-30 cm’s of recent HST made for great skiing on the south end runs. Mod-strong wind out of the south at 2350meters. Calm in the trees. Snowing S1 / S2 all day. No signs of instability observed today.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: We skinned up in the Helen Shoulder trees where it was snowing about 1cm/hr and an occasional wind gust could be felt. There was 5cm of new storm snow.  At the treeline, winds were much more prevalent, and after skiing a short run on the NE side, we skinned back up to the treeline to dig some snow pits. reports.title: Cirque Peak by Helen Creek
reports.comment:
quick: We skied the Cirque Peak North Couloir from Helen Creek yesterday. Same as the day before, the snow was nice and soft up to about the top of the "Katherine Ridge" (~2400m). Unlike the previous day, we got better views of some east aspects, and saw two big avalanches (size 2.5 or 3) off of Crystal Ridge. These both looked to be triggered by cornice failures, and within the last day or two.

reports.title: Crowfoot glades extended column
reports.comment: quick: While at crowfoot glades we did an extended column test at 2173M on an NNE aspect at 27 degrees. Had failure at 22 strikes with full propagation along the column. Snow depth was 143cm failure at 96cm. Continuous snow fall throughout the day. Amazing skiing in trees and open slopes. Witnessed and heard approximately 8 slides in the upper alpine on 60+ degree slopes on crowfoot.

reports.title: Cirque Peak Tour
reports.comment: snowpack: 2 separate pits failed on tap 2 at the base layer of depth hoar. It was a sudden planar cash registering effect.

reports.comment:

reports.title: Cirque Peak
reports.comment: quick: Had an overwhelming urge to do some digging today and wanted to check on how the persistent weak layers were behaving. We found the best skiing at treeline with boot-top pow, the alpine has seen a lot of wind. We avoided wind-loaded and convex features.

reports.title: Ramp Peak
reports.comment: quick: Skied Ramp Peak today. Cold, -15 parking lot and -25 up the valley. Sunny and light-no wind all day. Snow was minimally wind affected and offered deep powder with some sharks to watch for. A couple settlements were noted in low angle alpine terrain. Slab character was variable, with soft storm slab and hard wind slab near the top where things were wind swept.

reports.title: Katherine Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Toured up Helen Creek to the ridge where we skied down to Katherine Lake. Returned via Helen Creek. Skiing was good, snow is good in the alpine and better in the trees. Did a quick pit on a similar slope to our run. No result on a CT. / snowpack: CT no result. With the shovel I got a planar release on a layer at 45 cms. It was hard to get this to pop. 26 degree slope, NE facing.

reports.title: Mosquito Mountain
reports.comment: quick: Skiing was good enough on Ramp yesterday I came back today for Mosquito. -19 in the parking lot with a slight inversion in the morning. Sunny all day with a few clouds and light W wind. Mosquito was a bit more wind affected than Ramp (perhaps the former sheltered the latter from the SW winds?). Some very hard wind slabs near the ridgeline but powder was had a bit below it. Some bony section…

reports.title: Calm and surprisingly warm ( relatively)
reports.comment:

reports.title: Crowfoot Mountain/Little Crowfoot

reports.title: Sub Observations Trees South Aspect
reports.comment:

reports.title: Bow Summit Tour
reports.comment: quick: Gorgeous day out at Bow Summit today. Some pretty serious wind affect on the ridge and variable storm/wind loading on the skiable slopes. We skied three of the main chutes which held surprisingly amazing snow. No signs of whumpfing or instability. reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: -4 and calm at 0900hrs near mosquito creek hostel.  Good skiing in the glade and smaller avy path today.  Conditions are best 2100m and lower.  Found some reactivity on steep and convex features.  Cracking, small blocks coming off unsupported features at tree line.  Observed several recent up to sz2 from steep unsupported terrain above.  0 degs at 1500hrs at trailhead.

reports.title: Observation Subpeak
reports.comment:
snowpack: Really nice day at Observation.  Went up to about 2500m.  Practiced digging a pit at about 2300m on a 25 degree sw aspect.  CTH29 with a slight failure down 50cm.  No result on the ECT.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades

reports.title: Bow Peak, Crowfoot Pass

reports.title: Helen Shoulder

reports.title: West Nile

reports.title: Observation sub peak
reports.comment: quick: Saw a slab probably the Jan 11 layer from Wednesday from steep rocky unsupported terrain but no current signs of instability. Beautiful views, enjoyed the day, thinking positive until the next storm helps reset terrain.

Great conditions with about 15cm new snow on the old hard surface. Nothing observed all day. Did see old debris on the North side of Dolomite in the Ave paths off the steep unsupported slopes, guessing from a couple weeks ago.  Didn’t make it into the fan runout area so ver…

reports.title: Peyto Glacier/Mistaya Mountain
reports.comment: quick: Spent the last two nights on the Peyto Glacier. Snowed ~10cm Thursday evening/night with little wind which greatly improved ski quality on the otherwise heavily wind affected glacier. We made the slog over to Mistaya Mt on Friday under a strong cold W wind and mainly overcast. Nice powder on the sheltered glacier up to the col near Peyto Peak, but N from there it was extremely wind blasted …

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment: quick: Some pretty good ski quality on Cirque Forepeak today. Dust on crust, improving as we lost elevation. Some tricky skinning in spots with the surface snow bonding poorly to the disaster of crust, windblasted concrete and facets below it. Rocks in spots up high - had to be careful to not hit anything. Light winds, -19c start, -15c at the summit and -9c at the car. No instabilities noted where…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Great overall conditions - shoots are nicely filled in and the pillow lines are pillowy - lots of great options on the ridge and north glades. The snowstorm that came in today will add significant loading so take it easy in here over the next week and pay attention to tree wells, air pockets in the pillow lines, sluffs in the shoots, and releases off the east face of Crowfoot Mountain until…

reports.title: Bow Summit Study Plot
reports.comment: snowpack: Snow profile at the Bow Summit Study Plot

reports.title: OXO (Puzzle Peak)
reports.comment: quick: Skied OXO (Puzzle Peak). Mostly loose snow on the hard wind-scoured base, but the odd windslab on more east facing rolls. Snow is shallow in this area and a lot of rocks, many hidden by the new snow, so wouldn't recommend skiing here at the moment - much better below treeline.

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder Pow!
reports.comment: quick: Excellent skiing today with 25-30 cm of low density snow overnight. No slab yet below treeline in this area, but moderate SW winds had created slabs up to 1 m deep in lee features at treeline and in the alpine.  Some cracking observed when ski testing small windloaded slopes in the alpine.

reports.title: Too Deep
reports.comment: quick: Didn’t even make it to the parking lot in an SUV. Snow was silly deep, very slow travel and skiing because of which. Natural avalanches observed across the highway and in the Bow Summit alpine bowl

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Amazing quality skiing at crowfoot yesterday. Dug a pit on NE aspect that showed about 220cm snowpack with 70-80cm recent storm snow. ECT revealed no reactivity and no propagation. Saw some evidence of point releases from cliff bands in the alpine but appeared to be mostly storm snow sluffing. Still some lines left in the chutes! / snowpack: No results on ECT on NE aspect

reports.title: PaulR
reports.comment:
quick: Went out for a training day for aspiring ski guides, put on by Jordy Shepard and BCA. 

We skied up to tree line, and spent the day in low alpine terrain. We were careful to use terrain that posed minimal overhead hazards (some cornices in the area) and were mindful of the size and angle of the terrain we were using. We used some small rocky areas to practice technical rope systems. The ski…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr.
reports.comment: weather: Cold and getting colder. / snowpack: Obs in wind loaded feature near ridge crest. 15-20cm 1F wind slap over 50cm Fist snow sitting on old surface (dn 65cm). CTE(SP) 8,7 dn 20cm on PP and DF. CTM(RP) 18, 17 dn 40cm on DF. We decided to turn around and ski back through glades. Evidence of Cornice failure and old +24hr Na, Nc triggered avalanches size 1-2 on steep NE slopes off Jimmy Jr.

reports.title: West Nile Slide paths
reports.comment: quick: AST2 students report: Storm snow was denser than anticipated. No cracking/settlements/whoomphing. No natural avalanches. No reactivity while skiing up to 35degrees.  Pleasant day as long as you're out of the wind. View of ridge tops was limited, but we did not observe any snow being moved by winds.  North winds started around 3pm - potential for reverse loading if those winds move snow over…

reports.title: Bow lake
reports.comment: quick: Rode a NE fan across bow lake -30 at the car in the morning -14ish by the afternoon, calm, bluebird clear. Variable wind affect. on bow lake was hard non breakable wind crust, below the fan was thin breakable crust and between that we had some cracking and drum like sounds and then into and up the slope it improved to light powder. Observed surface hoar forming at valley bottom. Dug a pit a…

reports.title: Mosquito trees
reports.comment: quick: Quick walk up into the mosquito trees today temperature pretty cold but skiing good. pretty slow￼ with the cold temperatures. ￼￼ / avalanche: Well touring at the top of The ridge where it turns to Alpine, A natural cornice came down from the high cliffs above didn’t pull a slab though ￼￼

reports.title: Cirque Peak
reports.comment: quick: Made it about 2/3 of the way up to Cirque Peak.  Heavy-ish powder below tree line with 10-20 cm ski penetration.  Surface hoar at treeline in sheltered areas.  Heavily wind affected above tree line with 1-4 cm strong crust breakable in some areas where thinner.  No signs of instability.  Good skiing below treeline, but rocky, crusty survival skiing above. / weather: Clear, cold, and calm

reports.title: Dolomite Peak Circuit
reports.comment:
quick: Cold day in the alpine. Snow was crusty and slabby w variable loose pockets. 

Did not see any avalanche activity nor did we hear whoompf or sign of snowpack instability. All still look solid but will likely change w the expected warm up on Monday 15 onwards.  

Riding down the pass was poor. Some fun and turns to be had skiing down to the road for the last 1km or so in the trees on good po…

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: quick: Toured up Obs Sub Peak SW Ridge and over summit down to the Cirque/Obs Sub Peak Col. Lots of wind effect and scouring in the alpine made for highly variable skiing, with a mix of bulletproof windslab, windskins, and faceted sastrugi. No signs of instability noted. Not much recent avalanche activity apart from one recent size 1.5 slab in the North Bowl of Cirque Forepeak.

reports.title: Cirque peak
reports.comment:
quick: Skied crystal ridge to cirque peak, down the north couloir to the north glacier, went around the peak and finished with the dolomite circuit.

As others mentioned, variable conditions depending on aspects. A bit of wind crust. Of more note, the north couloir is pretty bare. We ended up having to rap twice to get past rocks - I’d only really recommend it as part of the loop and not for ski q…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Skied Helen Shoulder today. -17 on arrival, but warmed very quickly. Was -3 at the car when we got back. Sun felt very strong. North facing aspects skied well (25 cm pen). In an initial probe of West facing aspects directly facing the sun, found they were sun affected with a crusty slab about an inch thick on the surface.

reports.title: OXO Peak
reports.comment: quick: Beautiful day in the OXO/Puzzle peak area. -20C to start the day, about -8C by 4pm. Found plenty of alpine snow that was not wind affected, though exposed ribs and some slopes at treeline had areas of firm slab. Despite strong sun, there was nothing coming off the cliff faces on the upper face, and the snow stayed dry. Almost too dry in fact... the cold temps have left the snow quite grabby…

reports.title: Bow Subpeak
reports.comment: quick: SE shoulder of Bow sub peak from Mosquito Creek. Lots of facetting in trees and near shallow rocks/ridge. Main bowl is solid. Steep convex rolls at TL or just above were border line but they can be completely avoided. Some wind effects at TL and alpine on NE slopes below Bow Peak. Good snow in the main bowl.

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Skied Flower Couloir today with good stability in the couloir but poor ski quality. Our greatest concern was large, wind-loaded ALP features. / avalanche: One CS observed at 1030 just N of Flower Couloir. Located in steep, rocky terrain and likely failing on FC.  Otherwise no recent avalanche activity / weather: Increasing wind and blowing snow after 1200 with L SW winds gusting to M in the…

reports.title: Oxo - Puzzle Ramp
reports.comment: quick: Temperature is rising, may be an issue in the future. No signs of avalanche activity, mellow alpine slopes felt very stable with good skiing on faceted powdery snow. Plenty of room for fresh turns! Visibility with the light cloud coverage on open alpine was very flat.

reports.title: Crow foot glades
reports.comment: quick: No signs of instability. Very conservative day due to make up of the group. We road some of the glades. Mix bag varying from nice boot deep powder to to heavy and choppy conditions.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: We observed swirling winds with strong gusts from the N / NW. We had anticipated winds from the SW with the approaching storm system but where we were it didn’t materialize. Some isolated small wind slab formation observed on NW aspects (see pic). No whumpfing or shooting cracks, and the snow pit we dug showed no reactivity or fracturing in a compression test. Extreme swirling wind gusts an…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Rode crowfoot glades, stuck to mellow terrain. 
-8 at the car when we started at 9am. Warmer in the day but the wind was strong from the west. A lot of snow moving high on ridge tops around all day.
 The North side was good powder, protected from the wind but getting tracked out.
Wind picked up even more on the way out, gusts would almost knock you off balance skinning on Bow Lake.

reports.title: Dolomite Ridge Snow Profile
reports.comment: quick: Test profile at treeline on Dolomite Shoulder. Feb 19 facet layer below the new snow may become more of an issue as the storm snow settles. Lots of wind slabs present in the alpine and exposed treeline areas.

reports.title: West Niiiiile
reports.comment: quick: Chill half day at west nile. Few other groups with similar time to play encountered. Not as much fresh as forecasted (?2cm overnight) but still plenty of untracked to be had.  Wind effect and old debris above treeline.

reports.title: Dolomite Traverse
reports.comment: quick: Did the dolomite traverse Saturday. Several natural avalanches were seen in steeper but skiable terrain in the alpine. Including one that crossed the down track just after the transition. The ski track itself showed no sign of instability however it is a mellow angle for the most part

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Nice short tour. Well skinned track. Got some fresh tracks in, and saw 6-7 other groups. While climbing, around noon, we heard an avalanche in the high alpine running to treeline, but could not see it clearly. Our group well protected below the treeline on supported slopes.

reports.title: Bow Falls Ice Climb
reports.comment: quick: Skied in and climbed two laps of Bow Falls on Monday.  Clear in AM becoming very stormy as day progressed with falling/blowing snow, and non-stop spindrift. Very alpine feel! SIGNIFICANT- EXTREME CORNICE formation above climbs on far right side - Large growth in middle - no exposure once in left hand gully and climbing. No cornice dropping observed, only sprindriff/sluffs. Ice fair-great, s…

reports.title: Mt Gordon
reports.comment: quick: Went up Mt Gordon today. Coverage in the approach canyon is excellent.  A -17c start, reaching -7c on the summit and somewhere above 0 back at the parking lot. Mostly clear, some clouds around noon. Lots of wind all day, mod winds with strong gusts from the south, some blowing snow but it's been blown around so much already the plumes were quite small. Found easy travel all day with minimal…

reports.title: Cirque peak trees
reports.comment: quick: Went up the observation sub peak/cirque sub peak drainage with no real idea which runs we wanted to ski. When we got out of the trees we realized the sunny aspects where fairly crusty and not the best skiing. We skinned up to below some of the N facing chutes on cirque sub peak but didn’t feel great about the wind effect and cornices in the area. We finally settled on lapping a short run in…

reports.title: Cirque Peak Couloir
reports.comment: quick: 20 cms of spring pow over variable wind crust made for great supportive skiing on northerly aspects. Glacier was well covered up to 3 meters HS. Couloir is bony in top 60 meters still requiring raps or down climbing. 20-40cm Soft wind slab in immediate lee features that was reactive to hand and ski testing.

reports.title: Wapta and Mt Gordon
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the Wapta in a day and added in Mt Gordon  with my friends Leif and Joren.
The day was sunny and temps were -5 to -10 on the glaciers, but it was below -20 at the car at 7am.
Travel was great up high. Boot deep pow and most of the glacier/crevasses seemed well bridged.
There was point release on the east face of Trapper Peak.
Winds were high at ridgetop. / avalanche: A recent slab rel…

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Headed to West Nile planning to stick to trees. Looked up, it looked awesome. Decided to dig a pit at TL. Glad we did, stayed below TL. Note: traversed open roll to get a ‘better’ line....slid about 15 feet down slope on a layer 15-20cm down ~30 degree slope. Headed back to trees ASAP. / weather: Wind was calm until about 14:00hrs when it became noticeable from the south. / snowpack: Total …

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Did a few laps at Bow Summit at treeline. The area was very quiet. The light snow and wind gave the area a good refresh. We did not witness any signs of instability or avalanches. / weather: Morning was mainly overcast with light snow. Wind from the north west and was calm below treeline and was stronger at and and above treeline. Clouds burned away to a completely clear sky mid afternoon. …

reports.title: Dolomite
reports.comment:
quick: Dolomite cirque. 

Solar aspects (before 1pm) were motionless. Sticky surface snow (clumpy balls) under the skins was annoying but not terrible. No observed wet loose activity prior to skiing easterly aspects 

Pre-warming the treeline solar aspects had 10-20 cm of a pencil-firm “slab” atop rotten facets. Very supportive surface crust at the moment. Medium hand shear results. 

Late afterno…

reports.title: Cirque Peak North Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Our party of three skied the Cirque North Couloir traverse. We entered and exited near Helen Creek. Another party of three entered at Helen Creek and exited at Dolomite Creek.

Our party bootpacked all the way up Cirque Peak but the other party skinned on the climbers right snow-covered area, closer to the cornice.

We rappelled about 50 m down the couloir on 60 m ropes and found medium qua…

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak and N Glacier
reports.comment: quick: Beautiful day to be out on the 93N enjoying views. We toured up from the drainage between Cirque and Observation to the Sub Peak. We took the ridge route (includes exposure and the necessary mountaineering equipment is recommended) to the North Glacier. Turns on the north Glacier were variable but enjoyable. The exit was challenging skiing with sastrugi and hard surface snow, until the main…

reports.title: Mt Gordon/Wapta
reports.comment: quick: Skied Mt Gordon. Approach trail pretty chewed up & side cutt-ey. Excellent travel across the Wapta, probed consistently @ 275cm. No visible signs of sagging or holes of concern. We traveled as 2 teams of 2. -15 valley bottom at 5am, 4 degrees at 2pm back at the car. St Nich appeared scoured to rock. Snow was surprisingly pleasant, more powder than corn with highly variable wind effect.

reports.title: Bow Summit Study Plot
reports.comment: quick: Bow Summit Study Plot, No results on any snowpack text.

reports.title: Katherine Lake
reports.comment: quick: Rock solid icy crusty skin up to Katherine Lake but gaining the peak climbers from the col where you would normally ski down to continue dolomite traverse was worth it for some nice soft powdery turns (on top of a crust) despite the poor visibility. Solid crust in the Alpine, observed a couple 0.5 slides up high in the avalanche path crossings on the way back. Warmed up significantly once b…

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Toured up the stem and petals. Day started out mixed sun and clouds and turned to overcast and snow close to the end of our day, around noon. Noticeable sun crust in some areas. Couloir was hard pack from the middle to the top. Moderate boot packing. Skied one of the higher petals, lookers right. Noticeable sun crust, no signs of instability. Couloir is bad skiing up top but improved lower …

reports.title: Mistaya Traverse
reports.comment: avalanche: Numerous large sluffs and small avalanches off steep aspects of Mt Synge.  Poor visibility made it difficult to assess size and any propagation.

reports.title: OXO Peak
reports.comment: quick: Decent day on OXO. Lots of wind effect and some difficult up-tracking at times, but the face had better snow than expected. It may be spring in the foothills, but winter continues to reign supreme on the parkway!

reports.title: Ripe cornices, mushrooms and Avalanche
reports.comment:
incident: The trigger was likely a small cornice chuck that entrained snow from a ramp.  One person was knocked off their stance while boot packing.  Tumbling about 150-200m down the couloir, stopping on the surface, no injuries, poles lost.  Skis had been torn off pack and on the surface.
There was some space between party members that meant only 1 person was caught.  Helmet was of great value as…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Skied Bow Summit S glades today. 30-50cm new snow (230cm HS) & strong winds in the alpine. Intense periods of blowing snow, visibility akin to being in a ping pong ball. Storm snow interface failed CT10 un-clean "break" on compression test. However, no propensity to propagate on ECT. An unknown 2cm layer of small grain facets 70cm down was present, unreactive. No result on pit tests at this…

reports.title: Sitting Bull
reports.comment: quick: No signs of instability. Rode west aspects with 10-15 cm over bulletproof crust. Lee side of ridge developing wind slab.

reports.title: Crowfoot glades chutes 4/5/6
reports.comment: quick: Skied chutes 4-5-6 at Crowfoot glades today. Pretty epic snow conditions - fairly low density, no wind effect where we were (skied between 1950-2200m). Of particular note, significant sluffing with lots of entrainment. Bonding to prior interface was quite weak in steep terrain. Not super fast, but carried a lot of mass. We ski cut all of our entrances and they easily ran for 100m or more do…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Heard multiple avalanches off the steep slopes above crowfoot glade area. Unable to tell size based on visibility. Remnants of a recent small slab release below treeline on north aspect. Sluffing in steep terrain. Lots of new snow.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: avalanche: Two splitboarders triggered a slab avalanche as pictured around 1pm on March 30th. Snow, according to the riders, was powdery at the beginning of their run and changed into wind slab right at the fracture line. The avalanche ran out over the cliffs and into a terrain trap. One rider managed to get offside of the slide path, while the other gripped a small tree to avoid being pulled furt…

reports.title: Crowfoot trees
reports.comment: quick: Skied laps in Crowfoot trees and road facing chutes. Witnessed large avalanches coming off the headwall above Crowfoot Glacier and into the moraines below, all around 8am. Skied back to the car around noon and snow had become significantly wetter and heavier. No signs of instability in the areas that we skied. No issues with access/crossing the river.

reports.title: Katherine lake Helen ridge
reports.comment: quick: The alpine above Katherine lake was super wind affected. So was the backside of crystal ridge and everything we could see in the alpine.  We descended west slopes mid afternoon back down Helen creek, the sun had just come out and the snow turned super heavy and sticky. It was more work going down then up.

reports.title: Bow Summit Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Snow was wet and heavy below treeline early, around 10am due to warm weather overnight.

If the clouds and snow hadn't moved in by 11am we would have headed out early, as anything in the sun at our elevation was getting sticky and heavy. 

Fortunately, the cloud cover was thick after 11 and skiing remained good (and got better) as the snow fell and the cloud cover cooled things off. 

Small…

reports.title: Grand Daddy, fan
reports.comment: quick: We went up to take a look at Grand Daddy. We couldn’t see much in the couloir until we got up onto the moraines at the base of the fan, but there are some significant cornices that would dump into both the couloirs. We decided to work our way up the fan, avoiding potential runout zones for cornice debris and found OK/good skiing on lookers right of the runout. We didn’t find any wind slab o…

reports.title: Cornice fracture with small run out
reports.comment: avalanche: Small cornice fracture observed on the way up to bow hut this morning shortly after the sun peaked out from the clouds, obvious high winds at peak today as well.

reports.title: Crowfoot Couloir (fan)
reports.comment: quick: Broke a track up the fan of crowfoot couloir this AM. Turned around just shy of the couloir when conditions deteriorated with strong winds & a squall of fresh snow. A recent 10cm thick windslab had ripped mid way up the couloir, entraining loose dry & flushing out the lower half likely early this AM. Our concern was the remaining hangfire. Ski quality good on the fresh debris. Found soft cr…

reports.title: Cirque Peak/North Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Skied the Cirque North Couloir and took the Observation/Cirque drainage out to the highway. Stepped off at 9am from the Helen Creek trailhead and the touring snow/conditions were very stable. 6cm of fresh snow the night before made for easy travel. Once above treeline/alpine we had great weather with gorgeous views, but could see a storm rolling in from the northwest some distance away. A N…

reports.title: Crystal Ridge Slide
reports.comment: avalanche: A skier-triggered Class 1 avalanche occurred on the North aspect of Crystal Ridge in a steep alpine setting at 2pm (picture attached). The day contained rolling storms mixed with nice weather. We were exposed to about 30 minutes of sun before the run. We noted the layer of sun crust and quick change in the snow quality as we were heading up top for our second run. I predict the slide oc…

reports.title: Observation sub peak
reports.comment: quick: Beautiful clear morning on the parkway. -7 at the car at 7am. Went to N glacier on observation peak via the SE face/ east peak. West facing alpine aspects pretty wind blasted and bare up there. Upper pitch pretty wind affected, mix of dust on crust and sastrugi but lower down skied better than expected. Debris from an old size 2 noted on the SE aspect of observation peak near some cliffs. O…

reports.title: Funnel of Death Bow Peak
reports.comment: quick: Big hang fire cornice with a long crack behind it is currently sitting over Funnel of Death couloir on Bow Peak.  We went from the SW side to check it out this morning.  Part of the cornice fell sometime between yesterday afternoon and 11am this morning triggering about 2.5 avalanche.  Could see big debries on the fan and some slab crowns in the bowl below the cornice.  Lots of rock got rev…

reports.title: Bow Summit Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Quick trip up into the glades. Crusty leaving the parking lot. Conditions improve as you climb. But overall a dust on crust situation. 

New snow this evening may improve things.

reports.title: Ramp Peak
reports.comment: quick: The upper slope on Ramp Peak skied surprisingly well despite the western aspect and low light.  Limited wind effect and a firm slope brought ankle deep turns.  Shallow snow pack then exposed rocks near the summit so we ditched the skis and boot packed to the top.  Decent snow in the upper bowls below the main summit block and supportive crust through the trees above the campground.  A cool …

reports.title: Dolomite Loop
Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment: quick: Started cold, reached the sun just below Katherine Lake and it warmed up noticeably.  No instabilities noted on our trip but we saw debris from an avalanche triggered by a large cornice collapse east of Cirque Peak that slid over some ski tracks (background of 2nd photo).  We got out of the sun and into the trees above Mosquito Creek around 11 and although the sun was strong, the snow hadn'…

reports.title: Crowfoot
reports.comment: avalanche: Observed 3 size 1 and 2 size 2 loose wet avalanches within 15 minutes just after 10:00am. All started from rock bands on east aspects that had been in the sun for a few hours. As we skied down we observed about 10 more, including another size 2, over the next hour. Several had rock/dirt mixed in and we heard many more than we saw. Temperature at parking was -3 at 7:30am and +10 at 11:30…

reports.title: Large Bow Summit Avy
reports.comment:
avalanche: Slide happened sometime Saturday. 

Very large wet slab avalanche, looks to have gone full path and crashed into Peyto Lake. Estimated 20-30m wide and 2-3m deep where summer trail crosses the slide path above the lake. Ground vegetation exposed another 5-10m both sides of the debris. Possible start zone photos taken from Bow Summit upper lot.

reports.title: Large Bow Summit Avy
reports.comment:
avalanche: Slide happened sometime Saturday. 

Very large wet slab avalanche, looks to have gone full path and crashed into Peyto Lake. Estimated 20-30m wide and 2-3m deep where summer trail crosses the slide path above the lake. Ground vegetation exposed another 5-10m both sides of the debris. Possible start zone photos taken from Bow Summit upper lot.

reports.title: Mount Patterson
reports.comment: quick: Went up Mount Patterson today. Strong overnight freeze made for crusty travel (ski crampons mandatory) that was very slow to soften. 0 boot pen at 2300m at 1300. Many recent wet avalanches to size 2.0 observed, likely from the critical warming on Friday/Saturday (?). Only observed a pair of cornice failures trigger size 1.0 slides in extreme terrain. Bigger slopes felt quite locked up, espe…

reports.title: Cirque Peak North Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Completed the north couloir then traversed East around Cirque Peak. Overnight cool temps made for easy travel up to base of South ridge of Cirque. Sun effect on solar was just beginning to soften up around noon which made the final push up south ridge to couloir enjoyable with no ski crampons needed. The summer hiking trail still had blown snow filling it and was a great way to gain elevati…

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: Riding conditions were pretty good in the trees, in more open terrain it was still ok, but crusty under around 10-15cm of fresh snow, lots of signs of recent avalanche activity on solar aspects, and the snow started to be significantly impacted by the sun from around 2pm, temp had increased by around 10C from when we arrived to when we left. / weather: Mainly cloudy in the morning, the sun …

reports.title: Bow Falls
reports.comment:
quick: -5 at the parking lot at 6:30am
Very supportive snow pack throughout the day with 5cm of fresh snow overtop. 
No cornice above Bow Falls itself, although there is one that could partially threaten the approach slopes if you stray too far lookers right. 
WI4 with a thick eggshell layer on anything that is not vertical. 
Cornice collapse over what’s remaining of Gorby’s Falls. No other climbs…

reports.title: Observation Roadside
reports.comment: quick: Skied mellow w/NW slopes just south and below the alpine benches on observation. Above treeline was crusty will small amount of new snow on top. Treeline and below was softer with heavy, wet snow. Observed 3 older avalanches that had run on W/SW aspects towards observation peak proper.

reports.title: Gutentight couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Heavy sun affected snow from valley bottom up until the middle of the fan below the couloir.
Dry snow up the couloir a bit affected by various slide and sluff  that went down the couloir in previous days (like you'd expect in couloir like that)  
A relatively easy bootpack up (crampons highly recommended) and good skiing conditions.
Went up the couloir only until above the first rock band. …

reports.title: Grand Daddy - variable snow with cornice failure
reports.comment: quick: Solar punch was huge. Solar changing conditions in less then 10 minutes. Variable conditions from soft fresh snow to visible ice in the same turn. Backed off line at 3/4 of way up due to large cornice failure. Pooped our pants as cornice failed on adjacent coulior at around 825am. Better to drink beer then worry about the other bus size cornice above our head in the sun.  There is still a l…

reports.title: Cirque Peak N glacier
reports.comment: quick: Did Cirque via Num-Ti-Jah - didn’t see a soul as everybody was either skiing Hector or going towards Bow Hut. Fast travel on the MFCr. Ridge to summit looked bare (pic 1) but it was perfect on the up (pic 2). Didn’t use boot crampons but good thing the sun softened things up a bit for us. Rap was full 30m with a bit of a straight line (or use the intermediary anchor but it’s waaaayyyyhigh).…

reports.title: Saint Nicholas
reports.comment: quick: Can still connect the snow patches in the gravel flats past bow lake. Canyon travels well. Just a couple thinner snow bridges over the creek. Good coverage to bow hut. Solid crust today above 2400m on NE slopes till at least mid afternoon with approximately 10 cm of dry snow above the crust. Ski crampons helpful on steeper terrain.

reports.title: Mt Rhondda
reports.comment: quick: Skied Mt Rhondda yesterday, 6:32hr car to car. Around 1200m, 26km. Excellent overnight freeze, -9 at the car. Can still navigate the gravel flats with skis on, but hardly. Canyon coverage is excellent. Wapta saw 15cm of fresh + clear cold skis which made heavy surface facets & provided stellar riding conditions. Skin track took a bit more effort to punch, though. The new snow has concealed …

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Skied Observation Sun Peak Wednesday afternoon. This information is a bit old now but I figured it might still be useful to some folks. 

Weather was sunny and warm, calm winds with the exception of the occasional light breeze. Snow was isothermal at road level but fairly supportive in the alpine. No major signs of wet loose slides. West aspects above 2600m were still holding some relativel…

reports.title: Jimmy junior
reports.comment: quick: Went up Jimmy junior to ski some corn snow. We where a bit late but the slope was mellow enough that we weren’t to concerned although we did miss the corn snow and got some semi isothermic slush skiing instead which wasn’t ideal.
